Hi Tom / Sarah,

Thanks again for taking time today — really appreciate the candid discussion about Acme Bank's platform goals and constraints. I wanted to recap the key data-handling items we discussed and propose next steps so we can align on an actionable path.

Recap of requirements you mentioned:
- EU data residency for customer data and any persistent logs tied to EU tenants.
- PII classification: named entities in request payloads are considered regulated and should not leave the EU.
- Cross-region failover allowed only within EU regions; do NOT replicate primary data backups to the US.
- Retention windows: short-term logs (30 days) and audit logs (7 years) — details coming from your compliance team.

Immediate items / next steps:
1) Rishi (cc'd) will provide a technical note on how Redwood handles region pinning, backups, and cross-region failover.
2) I'll send our data residency PDF and SOC2 summary (attached) and flag the DPA addendum for legal review.
3) If helpful, we can schedule a 30-min technical deep-dive this week to walk your infra/compliance team through the architecture.

Please confirm if the above accurately captures your expectations or flag any corrections. Once we have Rishi's note, we can follow up with a single doc that your procurement/compliance teams can use to review.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0142

Hi Marissa — thanks for the recap. That captures things well. A couple of clarifications from our side: 

- EU residency: All customer content and any derived embeddings must be stored and processed in the EU. We can allow ephemeral inference in other regions only if no customer content or logs leave the EU.
- Backups: We require backups to stay in-region (EU) unless we explicitly approve geo-redundant backups to another EU region. No backups can be stored in the US.
- Failover: Cross-region failover within the EU is acceptable (e.g., eu-west-1 -> eu-central-1), but we need to know Recovery Time Objective (RTO) and Recovery Point Objective (RPO) for those scenarios.
- Logs/PII: Audit logs that contain PII must be redacted or masked; separate system-level logs that do not contain PII can follow normal retention.

Can Rishi provide the RTO/RPO numbers and the default behavior for KV cache and snapshot replication? Also, please confirm if you support region-pin at the account or project level.

Thanks,
Tom
Director, Cloud Security & Compliance
Acme Bank

Hi Tom / Sarah — thanks for the questions. Quick technical responses below; happy to do a screen-share to walk through diagrams if helpful.

1) Region pinning and account-level isolation
- We support account-level region pinning. When your account is created/pinned to an EU region set, all persistent storage (models, embeddings, customer data, and logs flagged as customer-specific) is provisioned in those EU regions only.
- Administrative metadata (non-customer telemetry) can be stored in a global control plane but is encrypted and access-limited.

2) Failover model (EU-only)
- Cross-region failover within EU: supported. We maintain active-passive replication with asynchronous block-level snapshots between primary and secondary EU regions.
- RTO/RPO: measured RTO typically 5–15 minutes for session rebuilds depending on model size and cache; RPO typically under 1 minute for request-level metadata and under 15 minutes for full disk snapshot replication in our standard configuration. For stricter RTO/RPOs we recommend Dedicated or Private deployments with synchronous replication options.

3) Backups & replication
- Backups are configurable. Default: daily encrypted snapshots retained in the same region. We can enable cross-region snapshot replication but only to other EU regions when configured. Cross-region replication to the US is not enabled for EU-pinned accounts.

4) PII / logging controls
- We support configurable redaction at ingestion for user-specified fields and a masking pipeline for common PII (emails, SSNs, credit card patterns) prior to any persistent storage.
- Audit logs that contain PII can be routed to your customer-managed KMS-backed bucket (EU only) or redacted before storage.
- Logs retention: short-term request logs default 30 days; audit logs configurable up to 7 years. We can set retention per log type per account.

5) Encryption & key management
- All at-rest data is encrypted with customer-managed keys (optional) or Redwood-managed keys. Customer-managed KMS/HSM integrations support EU-only key stores.

6) Operational notes
- In a rare full-region outage we will fail over to the secondary EU region. We can disable automatic cross-region failover and provide manual failover to control RTO.
- Disaster recovery snapshots are stored in-region unless cross-region replication to another EU region is authorized by you.

If this aligns with your needs, I can draft a short technical appendix with the exact RTO/RPO metrics and config knobs we would include in a Dedicated/Private offer. Would your team prefer a 30-min tech call or a written appendix first?

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
